name: VoltAgent
look: Void-black canvas with one electric-green accent, hairline-bordered cards and a dashed rule as the only ornament.

hero.title: The TypeScript framework for AI agents
hero.sub: Define agents, tools and workflows in typed code, then watch every step execute in a console that shows the actual reasoning rather than a spinner.

features.title: Typed agents, visible execution
features.sub: Everything an agent does is a typed call you can trace, replay and test.

items.title: Typed end to end
items.body: Tools declare Zod schemas; the agent's inputs and outputs are typed and validated at the boundary.

items.title: Visual console
items.body: Every step, tool call and token streamed into a local console. No print-statement debugging.

items.title: Workflows
items.body: Compose agents into supervised workflows with retries, branching and human approval steps.

items.title: Any provider
items.body: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or a local endpoint, swapped with one line.

items.title: Replay
items.body: Every run is recorded and replayable against a different model, so you can compare without re-running side effects.

items.title: Testable
items.body: Agents are ordinary functions. Mock a tool and assert on the result in your existing test runner.

showcases.title: See what the agent actually did
showcases.body: The console shows the reasoning, every tool call with its arguments and result, token counts and latency per step. When an agent goes wrong you can see the exact step where it did.
points: Token and latency accounting per call

showcases.title: Deploy it like any Node service
showcases.body: There is no proprietary runtime. A Voltway agent is a TypeScript module that runs anywhere Node does — a container, a serverless function, or a long-lived worker.
points: No proprietary runtime or hosted dependency

gallery.title: Documentation
gallery.sub: Quickstart, tool authoring, workflows and the observability protocol.

testimonial.quote: The console paid for itself the first afternoon. We found an agent silently retrying a failing tool eleven times, which no amount of log reading had surfaced.
testimonial.name: Jonas Lindqvist

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: The framework is MIT. The hosted console is optional.

items.a: MIT licensed, including commercial use, with no feature gating. The paid tiers add hosted trace storage and team features, not framework capability.

items.q: Does it lock me into a provider?
items.a: No. Providers are adapters; switching between OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or a local endpoint is a one-line change and the rest of the agent is untouched.

items.q: How do I test an agent?
items.a: Agents are plain functions. Mock the tools, call the agent, assert on the output — no special harness and no network required.
Locally by default, to disk, with nothing transmitted. The hosted console is opt-in and exports standard OpenTelemetry spans.

cta.title: Build your first agent
cta.sub: MIT licensed, TypeScript native, console included.

footer.tagline: The TypeScript framework for AI agents.

notes: One electric-green accent carries every CTA, status pill and the logo mark. There is no second accent anywhere.
The dark canvas is the only page surface — no light-mode rhythm, no alternating bands.
Hairline-bordered cards are the primary chrome: no shadows, no fills, just precise 1px rectangles.
A dashed rule between sections is the brand's only ornamental line. Use it sparingly as a rhythm cue.
Buttons are tight 6px rounded rectangles, never pills. Full pills are reserved for inline status tags.
